report_name: ToxicPanda 2.0 Android Trojan Enables On-Device Fraud

attack_patterns.name: GUI Input Capture
attack_patterns.description: The ToxicPanda 2.0 malware presents fake login screens that mimic legitimate banking or e-wallet apps to capture user credentials.

attack_patterns.name: Abuse Accessibility Features
attack_patterns.description: ToxicPanda 2.0 tricks the user into granting Accessibility Service permissions, which it then uses to read the screen, fill in text fields, click buttons programmatically, approve transactions, and grant itself additional permissions.

attack_patterns.name: Keylogging
attack_patterns.description: The malware monitors the device's lock screen to log the user's PIN or pattern, allowing the attacker to unlock the device remotely.

attack_patterns.name: Remote Access Software
attack_patterns.description: ToxicPanda 2.0 functions as a Remote Access Tool (RAT), providing a live feed of the device's screen to the attacker and allowing them to perform actions remotely for full control.

malware.name: ToxicPanda 2.0
malware.description: A sophisticated Android banking trojan and Remote Access Tool (RAT) designed for on-device fraud. It uses overlay attacks, accessibility service abuse, and PIN capture to take over banking and e-wallet applications.

tools.name: Android Debug Bridge
tools.description: The malware attempts to enable Wireless Debugging to gain a deeper level of control over the device via the Android Debug Bridge (ADB).

infrastructure.name: ToxicPanda 2.0 C2 Server
infrastructure.description: Attacker-controlled C2 server used to receive captured credentials and send remote commands to the ToxicPanda 2.0 trojan.

indicators.name: Programmatic Enabling of Wireless Debugging on Android
indicators.pattern:
title: Programmatic Enabling of Wireless Debugging on Android
id: 2b1f8c4d-9e0a-4b7c-8d1e-6a3f9b2c1d0e
status: experimental
description: Detects the programmatic enabling of the Android Debug Bridge (ADB) over TCP/IP, a technique used by malware like ToxicPanda 2.0 for deeper device control.
references:
  - https://www.malwarebytes.com/blog/mobile/2026/08/toxicpanda-2-0-can-take-over-your-android-phone-and-banking-apps
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-08-25
tags:
  - attack.t1623.001
level: high
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '/setprop'
    CommandLine|contains: 'service.adb.tcp.port'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects the programmatic enabling of the Android Debug Bridge (ADB) over TCP/IP, a technique used by the ToxicPanda 2.0 malware to gain deeper control over an infected device.
